title: Next-token prediction
note: text = subtitles; say = spelled for the voice. Numbers from brain3d/trace.json, films/qkv_data.json, experiments/logs.

blocks.text: Here is the whole idea of a language model. Text goes in, and the model predicts the next token.
blocks.say: Here is the whole idea of a language model. Text goes in, and the model predicts the next token.

blocks.text: It reads Emma's question, with the app's instructions in front: 100 tokens, in one pass. At the end of that pass, it gives a probability to every entry in its vocabulary, all 151,936. The top of the list looks like this.
blocks.say: It reads Emma's question, with the app's instructions in front: one hundred tokens, in one pass. At the end of that pass, it gives a probability to every entry in its vocabulary, all one hundred and fifty-one thousand, nine hundred and thirty-six. The top of the list looks like this.

blocks.text: We: 56 percent. As: 8. Manchester: 6. In: 5. The model is not certain. It is placing bets.
blocks.say: We: fifty-six percent. As: eight. Manchester: six. In: five. The model is not certain. It is placing bets.

blocks.text: One token is chosen and added to the text. Then the whole pass runs again, once for every new token. A few tokens later, the answer reaches its number. Now the bets are on a digit. One: 34 percent. Two: 21. Five: 12.
blocks.say: One token is chosen and added to the text. Then the whole pass runs again, once for every new token. A few tokens later, the answer reaches its number. Now the bets are on a digit. One: thirty-four percent. Two: twenty-one. Five: twelve.

blocks.text: Nothing here looks anything up. Every word of the answer, the number too, is a bet like this one. The rest of the lecture opens the box, to see how the bets are made.
blocks.say: Nothing here looks anything up. Every word of the answer, the number too, is a bet like this one. The rest of the lecture opens the box, to see how the bets are made.
